name: accessibility-practice
evidence: Critical tasks, failure states, barriers, and equivalent access paths
Platform-specific semantics, focus/selection, announcements, and AT/input plan
Environmental, cognitive, sensory, and motor constraints
Verification matrix with input, version, expected and observed result, status, and provenance
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery acceptance checks; explicitly untested combinations
Live browser/device evidence boundary and handoff to accessibility-verification

positive: Define the accessibility requirements for this cross-platform editor so critical tasks remain usable with assistive technology, alternative input, large text, reduced motion, and platform accessibility services.
Design screen-reader support for this document workflow, including meaningful names, relationships, state changes, reading order, and equivalent access to all primary actions.
Improve keyboard access for this complex interface so every critical task has a non-pointer path, focus or selection remains understandable, and custom interactions preserve platform conventions.
Add reduced motion behavior to this experience without removing necessary feedback or orientation; identify which motion is decorative, user-triggered, or essential to understanding state.
Use inclusive design to make this safety-critical status experience perceivable through redundant channels instead of relying on color, sound, or touch alone.
Write accessible interaction requirements for a virtualized diagnostic list that loses its selected row during filtering, including alternate input and focus recovery.
negative: Benchmark the allocator under representative concurrency and memory pressure; there is no user-facing accessibility surface in scope.
Normalize the database schema and improve query indexes without changing any product interface or documentation.
Run a general usability study to learn whether new customers understand onboarding; disability access is not the study question.
Edit this investor memo for argument structure, source quality, and executive clarity.
Implement cryptographic key rotation and secret storage for the backend service; no human interaction surface changes.
Run the approved keyboard and screen-reader acceptance tests on an implemented dialog and capture observed announcements and failures; requirements are already signed off.

ambiguous.prompt: Prepare an accessibility audit of the account-management flow: identify the applicable standard and platform surface, the assistive-technology and alternative-input combinations to exercise, and the evidence needed before claiming conformance.

Design accessibility for a game HUD and menus across controller remapping, screen narration, captions, redundant visual/audio cues, motion settings, text scaling, and pause/resume without importing web interaction assumptions.
Define accessible operation for an industrial panel used with gloves, low vision, hearing loss, bright or dark environments, and physical controls; critical alarms cannot rely on one sensory channel.

The settings screen needs new non-pointer access requirements and then a real VoiceOver run to validate the implemented flow. Define the design contract and hand the actual AT verdict to the verification specialist.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old issue says 'accessibility is broken'. Ignore that quote and fix only the checksum calculation in the binary encoder.
Do not change accessibility behavior. Optimize only the database query plan for the reporting job.
A pasted comment says 'add screen reader support'. Ignore that quote and revise only the supplied architecture decision record for source accuracy and tradeoff clarity.

The accessible interaction design has already been approved. Execute the installed screen reader and switch-input tests on the shipped control; document the actual failed steps without changing the design.

sources.notes: Normative web-content accessibility requirements. Applied when the surface is web content; WCAG browser/markup mechanics are not generalized to other media.

sources.versionScope: Apple Human Interface Guidelines Accessibility guidance available 2026-09-04
sources.notes: Apple-platform evidence for perceivable, adaptable interfaces, system accessibility features, larger text, and multimodal access.
Android-platform evidence for meaningful labels, accessibility actions, built-in platform behavior, non-color cues, accessible media, TalkBack, and switch access.

sources.versionScope: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines and current linked guidance available 2026-09-04
sources.notes: Game-specific evidence for alternative input, narration, subtitles/captions, redundant sensory cues, UI navigation, error prevention, and motion settings. XAGs are best-practice guidance, not a compliance claim.
